title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 104
paragraphs: From there they went on to invade Egypt; and when they were in Syria, which is called Palestine, Psammetichus, king of Egypt, met them, and by gifts and entreaties he turned them from their purpose so that they should advance no further. As they retreated, when they came to the city of Ascalon in Syria, most of the Scythians passed through without doing any damage, but a few of them who had stayed behind plundered the temple of Aphrodite Urania. This temple, as I find by inquiry, is the most ancient of all the temples that belong to this goddess; for the temple in Cyprus was founded from this one, as the people of Cyprus themselves report, and it was the Phoenicians who founded the temple in Cythera, coming from this land of Syria. So these Scythians who had plundered the temple at Ascalon, and their descendants forever after, were smitten by the divinity with a disease that made them women instead of men. The Scythians say that for this reason they were diseased, and that for this reason travelers who visit Scythia today see among them the affliction of those whom the Scythians call Enareis.
